a1_subject: Fatal exception condition (whether detected at compile time, circumstances under which detected)
a1_text: Fatal exception condition (whether detected at compile time, circumstances under which detected). This item is optional. This item if provided by the implementor, does not have to be included in the implementor's user documentation. (14.6.13.1.3, Fatal exception conditions)

staged_record.notes: A.1 item 69: 'Fatal exception condition (whether detected at compile time, circumstances under which detected). This item is optional. This item if provided by the implementor, does not have to be included in the implementor's user documentation.' (14.6.13.1.3). §14.6.13.1.3 (closing paragraph): 'If checking is not enabled for a fatal exception condition and the exception condition is detected by the compiler, the implementor is not required to produce executable code. It is implementor-defined which fatal exception conditions, if any, are detected at compile time, and the circumstances under which they are detected.' cite.py --check 14.6.13.1.3 'It is implementor-defined which fatal exception conditions, if any, are detected at compile time...' -> OK. No documentation duty. Determination as implemented: NONE are detected at compile time (the 'if any' arm) — executable code is always produced and every fatal condition is a runtime raise site. Probe fx.cob (OCCURS 5, constant E(6), COMPUTE X = 1 / Z with Z=0): without checking it compiles and runs (START / X=0 / DIV X=0 — the GR8 checking-off continuation); with >>TURN EC-ALL CHECKING ON it compiles and terminates at run time with EC-BOUND-SUBSCRIPT (fatal) — the compiler never withholds code, so no enabled-checking program is rejected. Exercising none of an optional latitude is conforming. No spec-derived test pins 'no compile-time detection' specifically -> empty test-ref (legitimate). Editions: exception conditions / checking are 2002+ (at 85 the latitude has no counterpart). || REFUTER UPHELD: Verdict and empty test-ref stand; the adjudicator's stated determination does not, and it must not be copied anywhere. A.1 69: 'Fatal exception condition (whether detected at compile time, circumstances under which detected). This item is optional. This item if provided by the implementor, does not have to be included in the implementor's user documentation.' (cite.py --check A.1 -> 'OK §A.1 69)'). §14.6.13.1.3: 'If checking is not enabled for a fatal exception condition and the exception condition is detected by the compiler, the implementor is not required to produce executable code. It is implementor-defined which fatal exception conditions, if any, are detected at compile time' (cite.py --check 14.6.13.1.3 -> 'OK §14.6.13.1.3 8)'; cite.py files this paragraph under item 8, not as a separate closing paragraph). The item is optional and need not be documented, so no DOC-A.1-69 row is needed, and there is none. The one hard constraint is the other way round: code may be withheld ONLY when checking is NOT enabled. Probes under /tmp/adj/refute-probe, each with >>TURN EC-ALL CHECKING ON: COMPUTE X = 10 / 0, DIVIDE 0 INTO X, MOVE 1 TO E(6) and E(0) (OCCURS 5), MOVE S(0:1) and S(4:5) (PIC X(5)), FUNCTION SQRT(-1), LOG(0), CHAR(0), DATE-OF-INTEGER(0), NUMVAL("ABC"), FACTORIAL(-1), INTEGER-OF-DATE(20231345), 0 ** -1. Every one compiles and ends at run time with the right fatal EC (EC-SIZE-ZERO-DIVIDE, EC-BOUND-SUBSCRIPT, EC-BOUND-REF-MOD, EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION, EC-SIZE-EXPONENTIATION). None is rejected at compile time. With checking off (fx69_off.cob), all of them run on to the end. §8.4.2.3.4 GR2 and §8.4.3.3.4 5b/5c are GENERAL rules, so constant out-of-range subscripts and ref-mods are not syntax errors, and accepting them is correct. REFUTATION OF THE NOTES: the claim that 'NONE are detected at compile time' is FALSE. ord.cob (ORDER TABLE OT IS "BOGUS-TABLE" + FUNCTION STANDARD-COMPARE) prints compile-time 'warning COBOLNET1662: ... Every FUNCTION STANDARD-COMPARE reference to OT will set EC-ORDER-NOT-SUPPORTED at run time'. That warning comes from DiagnosticCatalog.cs OrderTableUnresolved, EditionSeverity.Warning, and EC-ORDER-NOT-SUPPORTED is Fatal in Table 13. The program still ran and terminated with EC-ORDER-NOT-SUPPORTED (fatal), because §15.85.4 2) says 'the EC-ORDER-NOT-SUPPORTED exception condition is set to exist' (cite.py -> OK §15.85.4 2)). So at least one fatal condition IS detected at compile time, and code is still produced. That is conforming, since detection is optional and code is never withheld. The accurate determination is: 'compile-time detection is reported as a warning at most (for example COBOLNET1662 for EC-ORDER-NOT-SUPPORTED); executable code is always produced, whether or not checking is enabled'. The compile-time Errors that name run-time ECs (COBOLNET1688/1736 EC-PROGRAM-ARG-MISMATCH with AS NESTED; COBOLNET2113) enforce SYNTAX rules (§14.9.4.3 SR19/21/25; §14.9.39.3 SR30/34), not this latitude. No spec-derived test pins this item, so the empty test-ref is right. || Owning note: kb/Work/PB1535. || code-location commentary (registrar-normalized, kb/Work PB1522): src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/CodeGen/EcEmitter.cs#EcEmitter (fatal conditions always emitted as runtime raise sites | RAISE with checking off -> CobolFatalException, §14.6.13.1.3 #8)

staged_record.notes: A.1 item 72: 'FILE-CONTROL entry, ASSIGN clause (consistency rules for external file connectors). This item is required. This item shall be documented' (12.4.5 GR1). §12.4.5.3 GR1 b): 'A consistent specification for data-name-1, device-name-1, and literal-1 in the ASSIGN clause. The implementor shall specify the consistency rules for data-name-1, device-name-1, and literal-1.' cite.py --check 12.4.5.3 'A consistent specification for data-name-1, device-name-1, and literal-1 in the ASSIGN clause' -> OK §12.4.5.3 1) b). Row present: CONFORMANCE.md line 1607 '| DOC-A.1-72 |' — rule is textual sameness of the clause (same device-name/literal target, same data-name-1 spelling incl. qualifiers, case-insensitive), a difference raises EC-EXTERNAL-FILE-MISMATCH, storage for data-name-1 stays per element (GR3 b executor). Probes (two programs, one EXTERNAL FD, checking on in both): ASSIGN 'a-dat' vs 'b-dat' -> SUB=[EC-EXTERNAL-FILE-MISMATCH]; 'Data.txt' vs 'data.txt' -> NO-CONDITION (case-insensitive, as stated); USING FNAME vs FNAME -> NO-CONDITION; FNAME vs FNAMEB -> mismatch; fname vs FNAME -> NO-CONDITION. All five match the determination. Test: pb673_external_assign_executor pins the same-spelling/separate-storage/executor half from §12.4.5.3 GR3 b); the difference-raises arm for the ASSIGN target is probe-verified only (ec_external_file_mismatch pins an ORGANIZATION difference, GR1 e), not ASSIGN). Owning notes: kb/Work/PB673 (landed); PB685 (open) owns item 71, not this row. || REFUTED (CONFORMS -> PARTIAL): Owning note for the textual-sameness divergence: none (new; findings.json). A.1 72: 'FILE-CONTROL entry, ASSIGN clause (consistency rules for external file connectors). This item is required' and it shall be documented (cite.py -> OK §A.1 72)). §12.4.5.3 1) b): 'A consistent specification for data-name-1, device-name-1, and literal-1 in the ASSIGN clause' (cite.py -> OK §12.4.5.3 1) b)). The docs/CONFORMANCE.md row exists (line 1607). It states: 'COBOL.NET's rule is TEXTUAL SAMENESS OF THE CLAUSE ... every corresponding entry shall write the same device-name/literal target and the same data-name-1 spelling (qualifiers included), compared case-insensitively — and nothing more.' The implementation does NOT compare the clause text. The fingerprint (OoEmitter.cs EmitExternalDescribes, 'ASSIGN={f.AssignTarget.ToUpperInvariant()}|USING=...') compares FileModel.AssignTarget. That value is AssignTargetRule.Resolve's output: the device-class word (DISK/PRINTER) is DROPPED, and a literal is decoded to its bare text, so it matches an identically spelled device-name. Probes under /tmp/adj/refute-probe (gen72.py: MAINP CALLs SUBP, both with >>TURN EC-EXTERNAL-FILE-MISMATCH CHECKING ON, one EXTERNAL FD): c1 ASSIGN TO DISK "xa.dat" vs ASSIGN TO "xa.dat" -> NO-CONDITION; c7 ASSIGN TO PRINTER "xa.dat" vs ASSIGN TO DISK "xa.dat" -> NO-CONDITION; c2 device-name XADAT vs literal "XADAT" -> NO-CONDITION; c3 xadat vs "XaDat" -> NO-CONDITION. In each pair the clauses differ textually and the documented rule says they should mismatch. These cases agree with the documented rule: c4 USING FNAME OF G vs USING FNAME -> EC-EXTERNAL-FILE-MISMATCH (qualifiers included); c5 FNAME IN G vs FNAME OF G -> NO-CONDITION (normalized); c6 TO "xa.dat" USING FNAME vs bare USING FNAME -> mismatch. The enforced rule is a defensible consistency rule, but it is not the one documented: the published determination is inaccurate on the device-class prefix and on device-name versus literal. PRINTER vs DISK being consistent is a substantive rule a user cannot infer from the doc. Hence PARTIAL: either the row must say 'the same file-naming operand (§12.4.5.2 SR5 target as resolved by the DOC-A.1-71 rule; a leading device class is not compared; device-name and literal of the same spelling are the same target)', or the fingerprint must carry the written clause. Also note: case-insensitive literal comparison makes 'Data.txt' and 'data.txt' consistent, yet on a case-sensitive host each source unit's OPEN associates a different physical file (§12.4.5.3 3) a): 'associated with a physical file identified by the specification of device-name-1 or the value of literal-1 in the source unit' -> OK §12.4.5.3 3) a)). This is documented, so it is not a defect, but the row should say so. TEST-REF: pb673_external_assign_executor has NO >>TURN, so checking is off, WantsExternalDescribes() is false, and the fingerprint is never compared. It pins the GR3 b) executor association (the §12.4.5.3 3) b) half), not the GR1 b) consistency rule. ec_external_file_mismatch pins ORGANIZATION (GR1 e). No test pins item 72, so the test-ref must be emptied. || Owning note: kb/Work/PB1530, PB1535. || code-location commentary (registrar-normalized, kb/Work PB1522): src/Cobol.Net.Runtime (ExternalTable / FileConnector.Associate, SelectFingerprint via ExternalStore.Describe)

This alignment does not have to be documented' (cite.py -> OK §A.1 81)). §14.6.8.3 1): 'the content of the receiving operand is set to the algebraic value of the sending operand' (cite.py -> OK §14.6.8.3 1)). No documentation duty. The voluntary determination in CONFORMANCE.md §3 (lines ~592-619) says 'COBOL.NET performs the ISO/IEC 60559 conversion and keeps its result', that is, correct round-to-nearest. DEFECT FOUND — DOUBLE ROUNDING on the FLOAT-SHORT receiver. CobolFloat.StoreChecked(CobolDec, single) does 'double r = src.ToDouble()' and then narrows with (float); StoreSingleChecked(double) does '(float)src'. So a decimal sender is rounded twice, decimal->binary64->binary32. Probe /tmp/adj/refute-probe/fp81.cob: the sender is 1.000000059604644775390625000001, which is 1 + 2^-24 + 1E-30, strictly above the midpoint between 1 and 1+2^-23 (python Fraction check: x>mid True). The nearest binary32 is therefore 1.00000011920928955. For MOVE literal, MOVE PIC 9V9(30) data item, COMPUTE FS = literal, and the negative case, every 'FS->FL' shows 1 (or -1), at --std 2023 and 2002. The stored value is the binary32 FARTHER from the algebraic value, so the result is neither 'the algebraic value' as nearly as representable nor the documented 60559 conversion. The same code path also hits FLOAT-BINARY-32 (fb32.cob gives the same 1 results), where §14.6.8.3 2) mandates conversion 'in a manner consistent with the specifications of ISO/IEC 60559:2020, Clauses 3 and 5' (cite.py -> OK §14.6.8.3 2)). That is a hard sibling defect for its own row and needs a kb/Work note. These cases behave correctly: 0.1 -> 0.10000000149011612; 1.0E-50 -> 0 with no EC (checking off); 1.0E-40 -> subnormal 9.99994610111476E-41; -0.0 and ZERO -> 0; the out-of-range arm is as determined. Hence PARTIAL rather than CONFORMS. TEST-REF: the pb271_float_receiver_overflow header itself says 'the value below is a DETERMINATION and not a derivation'. It pins the §14.9.25.4 GR6 d)4.a out-of-range, content-undefined arm under checking off. It does not pin the in-range fitting ('alignment') of a value into a FLOAT-SHORT/-LONG/-EXTENDED receiver from spec-derived expectations, so the test-ref must be emptied. || Owning note: kb/Work/PB1110, PB1535. || code-location commentary (registrar-normalized, kb/Work PB1522): src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/CodeGen/Verbs/MoveEmitter.cs#MoveEmitter (float receiver store)

a1_subject: Implementor-defined exception conditions, EC-IMP-xxx (specification and meaning of xxx)
a1_text: Implementor-defined exception conditions, EC-IMP-xxx (specification and meaning of xxx). This item is optional. This item, if provided by the implementor, shall be documented in the implementor's user documentation. (Table 13, Exception-names and exception conditions)

staged_record.notes: Rule: A.1 99) 'Implementor-defined exception conditions, EC-IMP-xxx (specification and meaning of xxx). This item is optional. This item, if provided by the implementor, shall be documented' -> §14.6.13.1.6 Table 13 row 'EC-IMP-*suffix* (implementor specifies *suffix*) | Imp | Level-3 implementor-defined exception condition'. CONFORMANCE.md: no DOC-A.1-99 row, no statement of any EC-IMP suffix nor that none is provided. Code: ExceptionCatalog accepts EC-IMP-<any valid suffix> as an open family (like EC-USER-*), level 3, parent EC-IMP, fatality Imp which this implementation treats as FATAL; the runtime raises no EC-IMP-* itself. Probe p99 (>>TURN EC-ALL CHECKING ON; RAISE EXCEPTION EC-IMP-WIBBLE): compiles, 'abnormal run-unit termination: EC-IMP-WIBBLE (fatal): raised by RAISE and not resumed', exit 1. So the implementation DOES make a determination — every suffix is a valid name, meaning 'a user-raisable fatal condition the runtime never sets' — and it is undocumented => DIVERGES (silent). And if the intended answer is 'not provided', accepting an arbitrary EC-IMP-suffix is an under-rejection: Table 13 makes the suffix set the implementor's to SPECIFY, so a suffix never specified names no exception condition. No owning note (grep item 99 / EC-IMP-suffix in kb/Work: none). cite.py --check 14.6.13.1.6 'EC-IMP-*suffix* (implementor specifies *suffix*)' -> OK §14.6.13.1.6; 'Level-3 implementor-defined exception condition' -> OK. || Owning note: kb/Work/PB1531, PB1535. || code-location commentary (registrar-normalized, kb/Work PB1522): src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/Exceptions/ExceptionCatalog.cs#TryGet (EC-IMP- open-suffix arm, line ~250)
